clue.text: Aim to protest

definitions.meaning: an aim is a goal or purpose, the thing you are after
to protest is to raise an objection, to say you disagree

explanation.definitionFit: The noun sense is a goal or purpose; the verb sense is to voice disapproval, as in an objection.

clue.text: Securing ring, only one that French shop offered

indicators.note: the word for only holds the ring inside it

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
O is shaped like a ring
I is the Roman numeral one
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A French shop is offered only one ring to secure.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable shop.

clue.text: Notable failure to stop diamonds being lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word means reading it from the bottom up
the diamonds plug a gap in the failure, so go inside it

parts.note: a lapse is a failure
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A notable failure to stop diamonds being stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' tempts as stolen, but in a down clue it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means special or particular, so notable.

clue.text: Last man in trouble is taken in by a nurse?

indicators.note: the trouble goes inside the nurse

parts.note: to tend or nurse; a tender is one who nurses
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: The last man admitted in trouble is taken in by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a tail-ender is one of the poor batsmen at the end of the order; 'last man in' is the final batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the weak batsmen at the bottom of the order go in last, so last man in is one.

clue.text: Small amounts of water added to fresh, strong highball? Hardly

parts.note: drops are tiny quantities of water
hot can mean fresh (hot news) and strong (a hot curry)

explanation.surface: A barman adds a few drops of water to a strong highball whisky drink, so it is hardly a proper highball.
explanation.walkthrough: A highball is a whisky-and-soda cocktail on the surface, but here it means a high, looping tennis or badminton shot; the soft low shot that just clears the net is its opposite, hence 'Hardly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In racket sports a soft shot falling just over the net is the opposite of a high lofted ball, so 'hardly a highball'.

clue.text: Castigate male assistant when one's not suited to work

definitions.text: when one's not suited to work

parts.note: to dress down is to scold severely
a man Friday is a loyal male assistant, after Robinson Crusoe's servant

explanation.surface: A boss rebukes a male assistant for turning up unsuitably dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: On a casual workday staff skip business suits, so a worker is not suited; the pun is on wearing a suit.

clue.text: Assumption teacher supports endless homework

indicators.note: in a down clue the teacher sits beneath and so holds up the other piece
the last letter of the homework word is dropped

parts.note: prep is school homework, short for preparation
Miss is how pupils address a woman teacher

explanation.surface: The idea that a teacher backs unending homework.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiss is a proposition assumed as the basis of an argument, an assumption.

clue.text: Entirely without power, it's announced, for several days in spring

indicators.note: the words are heard spoken, giving a same-sounding phrase

parts.note: wholly weak means completely lacking strength

explanation.surface: A power cut lasting several spring days is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The week before Easter is set aside in the Christian calendar and falls in spring.

clue.text: Refuse to prepare bed

definitions.meaning: to refuse an offer is to decline it
hotel staff fold back the covers ready for a guest to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer; and to fold back bedclothes so the bed is ready for sleeping.

clue.text: Cheap tea, say, served in beaker with cereal

indicators.note: the tea is served inside the beaker, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking cup
the letter T is pronounced like the word tea
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A cheap cup of tea is poured into a beaker and eaten with cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold at a reduced or knock-down figure are inexpensive, the same as cheap.

clue.text: Merchant who makes first bid

definitions.meaning: a merchant is a trader who buys and sells goods
in the card game bridge the player who hands out the cards opens the bidding

explanation.definitionFit: A trader in goods, such as an antiques trader; and in bridge the player who distributes the cards bids first.

clue.text: They may have problems securing ride at the outset

definitions.text: They may have problems securing ride at the outset

indicators.note: the problems hold on to, so wrap around, the next letter

parts.note: hitches are snags or problems

indicators.note: points at the opening letter of the word ride

explanation.surface: Hitchhikers often struggle to get a lift at the start of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhikers thumb lifts at the roadside and may well have trouble getting one, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Watched film about sheepish type

indicators.note: the film goes around, so contains, the sheep

parts.note: vid is a short form of video, a film
a ewe is a female sheep, jokily a sheepish type

explanation.surface: Someone watched a film about a timid, sheepish character.
explanation.definitionFit: To have watched something is to have looked at or seen it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Robots with metal bars one fitted inside

parts.note: and means along with

indicators.note: the one is placed within the bars

parts.note: rods are metal bars
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Robots are built with metal bars, one fitted inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Androids are humanlike robots from science fiction, so robots is a fair broader term.

clue.text: A maid all excited about a religious leader

indicators.note: worked up and stirred about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A maid gets all worked up about a visiting religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges A MAID ALL into DALAILAM, and the final 'a' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Corporation finally dismissed inventive fellow

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is sent away

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch or belly

explanation.surface: A corporation finally sacks an inventive employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company but is the old humorous word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell, the inventor credited with the telephone, is an inventive fellow.

clue.text: British touring abroad on south Caribbean location

indicators.note: travelling around, so the letters wander about

explanation.surface: Britons touring abroad head south to a Caribbean destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Dissenter doing a demolition job?

definitions.meaning: one of the radical ... of the English Civil War, a political dissenter
one who flattens or razes buildings to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The 17th-century radical group who opposed the establishment; and jokily one who flattens, as a demolisher does.

clue.text: Hide, seeing young aggressive male?

definitions.meaning: an animal's hide is its outer covering or pelt
short for skinhead, a shaven-headed youth associated with aggression

explanation.definitionFit: A pelt or animal covering; and slang shortening for a shaven-headed tough youth, a skinhead.

clue.text: Get an unexpected kick out of this photograph?

definitions.text: Get an unexpected kick out of this photograph?

parts.words: Get an unexpected kick out of this photograph?
parts.note: a casual photo, but read as football: a quick, sudden kick at goal that takes the keeper by surprise

explanation.definitionFit: A quick informal photograph; in football also a sudden, unexpected shot at goal.

clue.text: Growth in furrow

parts.note: a crease is a furrow or wrinkle

explanation.surface: Growth appears in a furrow of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a rise in size or amount, a growth.

clue.text: Female, annoyin' tale-teller

parts.note: rankling, with the dropped g, means annoying

explanation.surface: A woman is annoyed by someone who tells tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Franklin is one of the pilgrims who tells a story in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Franklin, a landowner pilgrim, narrates one of the Canterbury Tales, so he is a teller of tales.

clue.text: KO'd very quickly?

definitions.meaning: knocked out, laid out on the canvas
at top speed, as fast as possible

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer knocked down lies prone on the canvas; and at full speed means very fast.

clue.text: We ably fixed rule

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We cleverly settled on a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges the six letters of WE ABLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A local regulation made by a council or company is a rule of limited scope.

clue.text: I'm coming in to complain about item brought back from abroad?

indicators.note: I'm enters the next word, so goes inside it

parts.note: to report someone is to make a complaint about them

explanation.surface: Someone arrives to grumble about something brought home from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that were exported and then bought back in are, as a noun, items brought back from abroad.

clue.text: Boy about to name English scientist

indicators.note: turns the boy around so his word reads backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy is about to name an English scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dalton, the chemist behind atomic theory, was an English scientist.

clue.text: To carry out garden task in summer is a bore

definitions.text: To carry out garden task in summer
definitions.meaning: to remove faded flowers from plants, a summer gardening job

explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners snip off spent blooms in summer; and as a noun it means a dull, tedious person.

clue.text: Southern vineyard given minute examination

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or its wine
minute, said my-NEWT, means tiny

explanation.surface: A southern vineyard is given a close inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like part of the phrase 'minute examination' but is tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Close careful inspection of something is examination; the answer is a synonym.

clue.text: Woman's part in Edwardian theatre

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is used, running inside them

explanation.surface: A woman has a role in an Edwardian theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a woman's given name.
